**Typecheck:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` → clean. Also sanity-checked `npx tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit` (governs `scripts/`) → clean.

**Live Binance recording:** Confirmed working for real — `npx tsx scripts/recordSample.ts btcusdt 8` connected to `wss://stream.binance.com:9443` and recorded **149 real live events** (105KB NDJSON) in 8s, verified by inspecting the file contents (genuine `depthUpdate`/`aggTrade` payloads with real BTCUSDT prices/update-IDs). Network access was *not* blocked in this sandbox, so this is a real, non-fabricated run. The sample landed in `samples/` (untracked, not git-added per your instructions since only `src/core/perf src/core/replay src/perf scripts` were staged).

**Key design calls worth flagging:**
- `RollingWindow`'s eviction test requires a sample to survive even though it's nominally older than the window relative to "now" at read time — the only consistent rule across all given tests is "never evict the single most-recently-pushed sample purely due to age," so that's what I implemented (documented in code comments).
- The Perf overlay sources its "message latency" samples from the shared `!miniTicker@arr` watchlist stream (`Date.now() - row.updatedAt`), since `DataHubClient` has no generic raw-message-timestamp hook — this gives real, always-available latency data regardless of which panels happen to be open.
- `scripts/recordSample.ts` declares a minimal local `WebSocket` ambient type (since `@types/node@20.19` doesn't yet type the Node-global `WebSocket`) rather than pulling in the DOM lib for a Node-only script.
